question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; breaking-design reassessment; Redesign from First Principles; hard-cut, ownership and type-boundary comparison
trigger: The user explicitly reopened the construction review under freedom to break and improve current APIs, challenging whether the previous Stop preserved current descriptor and configure semantics too readily. Assessment and recording only.
requirements: Required host resources must produce one complete installable descriptor with a fresh closure and Yjs factory token; incomplete definitions or factories must never enter plugin tuples.
The native factory remains the sole owner of the relationship between construction inputs and exact document, presence, compaction and cursor-data capabilities.
Plate adaptation and copied presentation composition must preserve that generic input-to-descriptor relationship without handwritten capability mirrors or generic forwarding overloads.
Author composition, terminal consumer overrides and external resource construction must remain distinguishable even if current method names and type states are allowed to break.
The target may add a primitive only when it removes current cross-layer coordination without adding editor state, runtime template lifecycles or package ownership inversion.
Existing shared descriptor ancestry, namespace admission, activation rollback, cleanup and exact portal lookup must survive every constructed result.
evidenceReuse: Reused matching shared-identity and collaboration production evidence only for existing descriptor and lifetime laws. Re-read current configure/extend and adapter types, the Plite private PluginTypeLambda precedent, native history/DOM/authored/Yjs constructors, Plate wrappers, Yjs's four Plate overloads, copied collaboration factory and 185 non-test configure call sites. The user removed compatibility and current-shape constraints, so the review explicitly reconsidered incomplete templates, descriptor-plus-options installation, capability splitting, editor-owned options and mapped callable factories. A throwaway type probe tested a derived single-signature Plate factory: direct option-specialized calls typed correctly, while generic copied composition lost awareness capabilities, proving a higher-order relation is required. The probe was removed and no product source was changed by it.
summary: Pursue a first-class mapped plugin-factory contract, while continuing to reject required construction inputs on configure or extend. Any options-to-plugin API is semantically a factory; hiding it behind YjsPlugin.configure does not remove construction and gives configure a second job. The stronger target keeps callable factories but adds a private input-to-exact-descriptor witness and result mapping, so native yjs can be adapted by Plate and then copied UI without Plate redeclaring API groups, four capability overloads or another generic forwarding function. Unlike an incomplete plugin template, factory mapping adds no install state or editor runtime owner and every call still returns one complete nominal descriptor.
alternatives: Keep handwritten createYjsPlugin and createCollaborationPlugin: runtime-correct baseline, but rejects the available owner repair and leaves native capability shapes and generic forwarding duplicated across two layers.

Bind resources with YjsPlugin.configure: reject even under breaking freedom because configure already owns terminal consumer overrides, while an unbound YjsPlugin requires a second non-installable template state or unsafe installation.
Bind resources through extend: reject because imported author contribution and externally owned runtime construction remain distinct jobs in the ideal model.

Make every plugin a definition plus descriptor/options install tuple: reject because it taxes static plugins and descriptor lookup, yet still requires the same dependent input-to-capability relation for copied composition.
Split Yjs base, presence and compaction into separate plugins: reject because fixed capability types add coordination around one namespace, binding, admission and cleanup lifetime.
Move plugin options to createEditor: reject because descriptor-keyed editor configuration relocates construction, weakens local discoverability and does not remove generic specialization.

Add a callable PluginFactory with a private input-to-descriptor witness and result mapper: selected because it derives cross-layer factories without adding installable incomplete values or runtime state.
Only derive a local return type with ReturnType or a cast: insufficient; the probe preserved direct calls but lost awareness through the current generic copied preset.
proofLimits: Source-backed Pursue verdict, not an accepted signature or implementation. The throwaway compile establishes that naive inference is insufficient; it does not prove a particular higher-kinded encoding, mapping syntax, declaration shape or cost. No factory-mapping candidate was implemented, emitted, benchmarked or exercised at runtime. Design must compare a private witness plus standalone mapper against a callable factory with map, prove direct and copied validators and absent capabilities, preserve fresh descriptor/token identity and ancestry, and measure declaration size, TypeScript cost, DCE and runtime construction. Existing collaboration behavior remains proven only by its prior record.
